trial_court: Court of Learned District Judge, Family Court, Bhiwani

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: wife, seeking transfer of petition filed by husband

acts_cited_auto: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

acts_cited.act: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

facts_of_case: Petitioner-wife seeks transfer of petition filed by respondent-husband under Hindu Marriage Act, citing distance and hardship in traveling from Bhiwani to Gurugram.

legal_principles.principle: The cardinal principle for exercise of power under section 24 of the Code of Civil Procedure is that the ends of justice should demand the transfer of the suit, appeal or other proceeding.
legal_principles.held: The cardinal principle for exercise of power under section 24 of the Code of Civil Procedure is that the ends of justice should demand the transfer of the suit, appeal or other proceeding.
cited_cases: N.C.V. Aishwarya v. A.S. Saravana Karthik Sha, AIR 2022 SC 4318

legal_principles.principle: In matrimonial matters, the Courts have to take into consideration the economic soundness of both parties, the social strata of the spouses and their behavioural pattern.
legal_principles.held: In matrimonial matters, wherever Courts are called upon to consider the plea of transfer, the Courts have to take into consideration the economic soundness of both the parties, the social strata of the spouses and their behavioural pattern
applicable_acts_sections: Code of Civil Procedure — Section Y
cited_cases: N.C.V. Aishwarya v. A.S. Saravana Karthik Sha, AIR 2022 SC 4318

legal_principles.principle: The Courts should give more weightage and consideration to the convenience of the female litigants and transfer of legal proceedings from one court to another.
legal_principles.held: Further, Hon'ble the Apex Court in Rajani Kishor Pradeshi v. Kishor Babulal Pardeshi, (2005) 12 SCC 237, has observed that 'while deciding the transfer application, the Courts are required to give more weightage and consideration to the convenience of the female litigants and transfer of legal proceedings from one court to another.'
applicable_acts_sections: Code of Civil Procedure — Section X
Protection of Women from DV Act — Section Y
cited_cases: Rajani Kishor Pradeshi v. Kishor Babulal Pardeshi, (2005) 12 SCC 237

legal_principles.principle: The Courts should ensure that leniency given to the female litigants should not be misused.
legal_principles.held: However, to avoid any misuse of the lenient view by the female litigants, Hon'ble the Apex Court in Anindita Das v. Srijit Das, (2006) 9 SCC 197, has also cautioned that 'the Courts should ensure that such leniency given to the female litigants should not be misused.'
applicable_acts_sections: Code of Civil Procedure — Section X
Protection of Women from DV Act — Section Y
cited_cases: Anindita Das v. Srijit Das, (2006) 9 SCC 197

outcome.final_order: The court allows the transfer application and directs the petition be transferred to any Court of competent jurisdiction at Gurugram.
